significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that a "compact feature set" in teacher activations predicts per-sequence transmissibility and that clamping it "monotonically increases or removes" the acquired trait, combining a form-(iii) predictive/dose-response relation with form-(ii) causal mediation. This would establish both a phenomenon—transmission strength varies predictably with feature activity—and a generation-side mechanism that fixes which sequences should transmit and how student behavior should change under feature amplification or suppression, although it would not explain how the student decodes the signal. The semantic and behavioral controls reported in Cloud et al., "Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data" (2025), make the internal encoding of the generated payload a live explanatory gap; a negative result would distinguishably reject the compact SAE-mediated account in favor of a diffuse or differently represented channel, though it would not rule out every low-dimensional mechanism. In the topic-substitution check, merely proposing to extend subliminal-learning research would not earn this score; the predictive coupling, monotonic intervention relation, and trait-specific mediation are the claim-specific reasons it rises above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handles are feature activity that "predicts which sequences transmit" and a "generation-side control for stopping unwanted trait leakage" by clamping the implicated features. These are ex ante handles: after calibration, outputs can be screened or modified before they are used to fine-tune a student, giving distillation auditors and model operators an action window rather than only a post-hoc explanation. The asserted conclusion covers ostensibly neutral outputs such as "numbers/code" and potentially multiple traits, but it does not assert architecture-wide transfer; because an SAE must be trained for the specific teacher, a new model requires re-extraction, with the compact-set and monotonic relations predicted more clearly than the identities of the features themselves. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the topic alone supplies neither an advance-warning diagnostic nor an intervention, whereas this claim specifically hands both to downstream users.
